You are auditing part of an "Agentic Design Workflow" repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover — a client design/handover project for "Zimmermann" (fashion retail website redesign, component prefix "zimm", target stacks web+react, initiated 2026-07-08 by Alrick Pagnon). This is a READ-ONLY audit — do not modify any files.

Scope: `01-context/`, `03-requirements/`, `04-feedback/`, `05-handover/`, `06-tools/`, and these root-level files: `project.config.js`, `AGENTS.md`, `.antigravity.md`, `COLLABORATION.md`, `README.md`, `vercel.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/mcp.json`, and the shell scripts in `.claude/git-hooks/` (`guard-bash.sh`, `guard-write.sh`, `on-write.sh`, `post-commit`, `pre-push`).

Context: `01-context/project-context.md` is a synthesis layer meant to be built by an `/update-context` skill from reference materials — it is currently unpopulated (placeholder only). `03-requirements/{epics,features,stories}/` is BA/PM-owned and independent of the design track. `04-feedback/` holds Figma comment exports from a `/capture-feedback` skill. `05-handover/index.md` is the engineering handover entry point, managed by a `/handover` skill — as of last check it was still the raw unfilled template (literal placeholder text like `[Project Name]`, `[Client]`). `AGENTS.md` and `.antigravity.md` are meant to mirror the same project context as the root `CLAUDE.md` for other AI tools (Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity) — they may legitimately stay generic/template, or may have been updated; just report their actual state, don't assume either is "correct."

Your job:

1. Confirm `01-context/`, `03-requirements/`, `04-feedback/` are genuinely empty/unpopulated (only `.gitkeep` files, template placeholders) as expected at this early project stage, vs. containing any stray/orphaned real content that isn't reflected in `01-context/project-context.md`'s manifest.
2. Read `05-handover/index.md` in full and list exactly which placeholder fields remain unfilled (e.g. `[Project Name]`, `[Client]`, `[Lead]`, `[Stacks]`, the Build Status line, etc.).
3. Check `06-tools/markitdown-mcp/`: is it a real, complete vendored MCP server (check `pyproject.toml`, the `src/` tree has actual source, `tests/` isn't empty-stub) or just placeholder scaffolding? Then check `.claude/mcp.json` — does it actually register/point to this server correctly (do referenced paths exist)?
4. Skim `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` for anything concretely off — accidentally committed secrets/tokens, unusually broad permissions, dangling references. This is a light scan, not a deep security audit; only report concrete issues, not general observations.
5. Read each script in `.claude/git-hooks/` (`guard-bash.sh`, `guard-write.sh`, `on-write.sh`, `post-commit`, `pre-push`) and summarize what each does in one line. Flag if any references a file path or command that doesn't exist in this repo.
6. Skim `vercel.json`, `README.md`, and `COLLABORATION.md` for leftover generic placeholder text that `/initiate-design-project` should have replaced with Zimmermann-specific content but apparently didn't.
7. Sanity-check `project.config.js` values you can verify against reality — e.g. does `componentPrefix: "zimm"` actually match the prefix used in `02-design/library/elements/*` files? (You don't need to deep-audit the library itself, another agent covers that — just this one cross-check.)

Report back in under 550 words: a findings list grouped as "Expected-empty confirmed / anomalies", "Handover template gaps", "Tooling & MCP wiring", "Config/secrets scan", and "Git hooks summary" (one line per script), each item as `path — one-sentence description`. State plainly if a section had no issues. Do not propose or apply fixes, this is audit only.

# Platform Base Layer: Web

- Minimum touch target for pointer/touch dual-use surfaces: 44x44px.
- Custom fonts require FOUT/FOIT handling. Specify `font-display` strategy in the spec.

---

| Name | Min width | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile | 360px | Default, designed first |
| Tablet | 768px | |
| Desktop | 1280px | |
| Wide | 1440px | Optional |

Set target browsers in `project.config.js`. The `/extract-specs` skill flags any CSS or JS used in a prototype that is not supported by the stated targets and prompts the designer to note a fallback.

Common degradation patterns to anticipate:

| Feature | Baseline | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Container queries | Baseline 2023 | Media queries |
| `@layer` | Baseline 2022 | Manual specificity |
| `:has()` | Baseline 2023 | JS class toggle |
| View Transitions API | Partial | CSS transition fallback |
| `color-mix()` | Baseline 2023 | Static colour value |

# MarkItDown-MCP

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The MarkItDown-MCP package is meant for **local use**, with local trusted agents. In particular, when running the MCP server with Streamable HTTP or SSE, it binds to `localhost` by default, and is not exposed to other machines on the network or Internet. In this configuration, it is meant to be a direct alternative to the STDIO transport, which may be more convenient in some cases. DO NOT bind the server to other interfaces unless you understand the [security implications](#security-considerations) of doing so.


[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/markitdown-mcp.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/markitdown-mcp/)
![PyPI - Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dd/markitdown-mcp)
[![Built by AutoGen Team](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20by-AutoGen%20Team-blue)](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen)

The `markitdown-mcp` package provides a lightweight STDIO, Streamable HTTP, and SSE MCP server for calling MarkItDown.

It exposes one tool: `convert_to_markdown(uri)`, where uri can be any `http:`, `https:`, `file:`, or `data:` URI.

## Installation

To install the package, use pip:

```bash
pip install markitdown-mcp
```

## Usage

To run the MCP server, using STDIO (default), use the following command:


```bash	
markitdown-mcp
```

To run the MCP server, using Streamable HTTP and SSE, use the following command:

```bash	
markitdown-mcp --http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3001
```

## Running in Docker

To run `markitdown-mcp` in Docker, build the Docker image using the provided Dockerfile:
```bash
docker build -t markitdown-mcp:latest .
```

And run it using:
```bash
docker run -it --rm markitdown-mcp:latest
```
This will be sufficient for remote URIs. To access local files, you need to mount the local directory into the container. For example, if you want to access files in `/home/user/data`, you can run:

```bash
docker run -it --rm -v /home/user/data:/workdir markitdown-mcp:latest
```

Once mounted, all files under data will be accessible under `/workdir` in the container. For example, if you have a file `example.txt` in `/home/user/data`, it will be accessible in the container at `/workdir/example.txt`.

## Accessing from Claude Desktop

It is recommended to use the Docker image when running the MCP server for Claude Desktop.

Follow [these instructions](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/quickstart/user#for-claude-desktop-users) to access Claude's `claude_desktop_config.json` file.

Edit it to include the following JSON entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "markitdown": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--rm",
        "-i",
        "markitdown-mcp:latest"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

If you want to mount a directory, adjust it accordingly:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "markitdown": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
	"run",
	"--rm",
	"-i",
	"-v",
	"/home/user/data:/workdir",
	"markitdown-mcp:latest"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Debugging

To debug the MCP server you can use the `MCP Inspector` tool.

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
```

You can then connect to the inspector through the specified host and port (e.g., `http://localhost:5173/`).

If using STDIO:
* select `STDIO` as the transport type,
* input `markitdown-mcp` as the command, and
* click `Connect`

If using Streamable HTTP:
* select `Streamable HTTP` as the transport type,
* input `http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp` as the URL, and
* click `Connect`

If using SSE:
* select `SSE` as the transport type,
* input `http://127.0.0.1:3001/sse` as the URL, and
* click `Connect`

Finally:
* click the `Tools` tab,
* click `List Tools`,
* click `convert_to_markdown`, and
* run the tool on any valid URI.

## Security Considerations

The server does not support authentication, and runs with the privileges of the user running it. For this reason, when running in SSE or Streamable HTTP mode, the server binds by default to `localhost`. If you require additional security, consider running the server in a sandboxed environment, such as a virtual machine or container, and ensure that the user permissions are properly configured to limit access to sensitive files and network segments. - **Available as a tool:** Any skill or agent can call MarkItDown to convert documents on demand.

The MCP server is vendored inside ADW at `06-tools/markitdown-mcp/`. On first project open:

1. Claude Code (or your AI tool) will detect the `.claude/mcp.json` config.
2. It will prompt you to install dependencies for the MCP server.
3. Confirm, and the tool will install `markitdown_mcp` and its dependencies automatically.
4. Done. MarkItDown is now available to all skills and agents.

- **Documents:** PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, DOC, XLS, PPT, EPUB, ZIP
- **Images:** JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP (with OCR if enabled)
- **Audio:** MP3, WAV, M4A (with speech-to-text if enabled)
- **Web:** HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, YouTube URLs
- **Text:** Plain text, Markdown, plain text versions of other formats

- MarkItDown source: `06-tools/markitdown-mcp/`

import contextlib
import sys
import os
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from mcp.server.sse import SseServerTransport
from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.routing import Mount, Route
from starlette.types import Receive, Scope, Send
from mcp.server import Server
from mcp.server.streamable_http_manager import StreamableHTTPSessionManager
from markitdown import MarkItDown
import uvicorn

# Initialize FastMCP server for MarkItDown (SSE)
mcp = FastMCP("markitdown")


@mcp.tool()
async def convert_to_markdown(uri: str) -> str:
    """Convert a resource described by an http:, https:, file: or data: URI to markdown"""
    return MarkItDown(enable_plugins=check_plugins_enabled()).convert_uri(uri).markdown


def check_plugins_enabled() -> bool:
    return os.getenv("MARKITDOWN_ENABLE_PLUGINS", "false").strip().lower() in (
        "true",
        "1",
        "yes",
    )


def create_starlette_app(mcp_server: Server, *, debug: bool = False) -> Starlette:
    sse = SseServerTransport("/messages/")
    session_manager = StreamableHTTPSessionManager(
        app=mcp_server,
        event_store=None,
        json_response=True,
        stateless=True,
    )

    async def handle_sse(request: Request) -> None:
        async with sse.connect_sse(
            request.scope,
            request.receive,
            request._send,
        ) as (read_stream, write_stream):
            await mcp_server.run(
                read_stream,
                write_stream,
                mcp_server.create_initialization_options(),
            )

    async def handle_streamable_http(
        scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send
    ) -> None:
        await session_manager.handle_request(scope, receive, send)

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: Starlette) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        """Context manager for session manager."""
        async with session_manager.run():
            print("Application started with StreamableHTTP session manager!")
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                print("Application shutting down...")

    return Starlette(
        debug=debug,
        routes=[
            Route("/sse", endpoint=handle_sse),
            Mount("/mcp", app=handle_streamable_http),
            Mount("/messages/", app=sse.handle_post_message),
        ],
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )


# Main entry point
def main():
    import argparse

    mcp_server = mcp._mcp_server

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run a MarkItDown MCP server")

    parser.add_argument(
        "--http",
        action="store_true",
        help="Run the server with Streamable HTTP and SSE transport rather than STDIO (default: False)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--sse",
        action="store_true",
        help="(Deprecated) An alias for --http (default: False)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--host", default=None, help="Host to bind to (default: 127.0.0.1)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--port", type=int, default=None, help="Port to listen on (default: 3001)"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    use_http = args.http or args.sse

    if not use_http and (args.host or args.port):
        parser.error(
            "Host and port arguments are only valid when using streamable HTTP or SSE transport (see: --http)."
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    if use_http:
        host = args.host if args.host else "127.0.0.1"
        if args.host and args.host not in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost"):
            print(
                "\n"
                "WARNING: The server is being bound to a non-localhost interface "
                f"({host}).\n"
                "This exposes the server to other machines on the network or Internet.\n"
                "The server has NO authentication and runs with your user's privileges.\n"
                "Any process or user that can reach this interface can read files and\n"
                "fetch network resources accessible to this user.\n"
                "Only proceed if you understand the security implications.\n",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        starlette_app = create_starlette_app(mcp_server, debug=True)
        uvicorn.run(
            starlette_app,
            host=host,
            port=args.port if args.port else 3001,
        )
    else:
        mcp.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    ]

    for pattern, message in destructive:
        if re.search(pattern, command):
            print(f"ADW blocked: {message} Confirm this is intentional before proceeding.")
            sys.exit(1)

except Exception:
    pass

sys.exit(0)

    if any(t in path for t in triggers):
        with open('01-context/.pending-update', 'a') as f:

    # 2. intent.md: check linked spec exists
    if path.endswith('intent.md') and '02-design/prototypes/' in path:
        spec_match = re.search(r'^spec:\s*(.+)$', content, re.MULTILINE)
        if spec_match:
            spec_rel = spec_match.group(1).strip().strip('"\'')
            spec_path = os.path.join('02-design/specs', spec_rel)
            if not os.path.exists(spec_path):
                print(f"ADW: intent.md links to '{spec_path}' which does not exist yet. Create the spec before running /handover.")

    if path.endswith('02-design/library/tokens.md') or '/02-design/library/tokens.md' in path:
        print("ADW: tokens.md updated. Run /extract to sync CSS variables in common.css.")

    if '02-design/specs/' in path and path.endswith('.md'):
        try:

#!/bin/bash
# ADW pre-push hook.
# Warns if any prototype has been updated more recently than its linked spec.

STALE=()

while IFS= read -r intent; do
    dir=$(dirname "$intent")
    spec=$(grep -m1 '^spec:' "$intent" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/spec: *//' | tr -d '"'"'")

    if [ -n "$spec" ]; then
        spec_path="02-design/specs/$spec"
        if [ -f "$spec_path" ]; then
            proto_time=$(git log -1 --format="%ct" -- "$dir/" 2>/dev/null)
            spec_time=$(git log -1 --format="%ct" -- "$spec_path" 2>/dev/null)
            if [ -n "$proto_time" ] && [ -n "$spec_time" ] && [ "$proto_time" -gt "$spec_time" ]; then
                age=$(git log -1 --format="%cr" -- "$dir/")
                STALE+=("$spec_path (prototype updated $age)")
            fi
        fi
    fi
done < <(find 02-design/prototypes -name "intent.md" 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#STALE[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "ADW: These specs may be stale — prototype updated after last spec commit:"
    for item in "${STALE[@]}"; do
        echo "  - $item"
    done
    echo ""
    printf "Push anyway? (y/n) "
    read -r answer < /dev/tty
    if [ "$answer" != "y" ] && [ "$answer" != "Y" ]; then
        echo "Push cancelled."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

exit 0

# Working together on this project: a guide for designers

This project lives on **GitHub**, a shared team home for all our files. This guide
explains how it works and what to do day to day. You don't need to learn any technical
commands. You'll mostly just talk to **Claude Code** in plain English. The example
phrases below are exactly what you can type.

---

## The big idea

GitHub is like a shared team home for our files, but much safer than Dropbox or Google
Drive. The key difference: **you never edit the shared master directly.** You take your
own private copy, make your changes there, then propose them back to the team. Nothing
you do can break anyone else's work, and nothing is ever truly lost. GitHub keeps a
complete history of every version.

If you've used **branching in Figma** (make a branch, work on it, merge it back after
review) this is exactly the same idea, for our project files.

---

## The words you'll hear

You don't need to memorise these, but so they're not mysterious:

- **Repo:** the shared project home on GitHub (the "master").
- **Clone:** making your own local copy the very first time (one-off setup).
- **Branch:** your private working copy. Like a Figma branch: experiment freely, the
  main version stays untouched.
- **Commit:** saving a labelled checkpoint, with a short note on what you did.
- **Push:** uploading your checkpoints to GitHub so they're backed up and visible.
- **Pull:** grabbing everyone else's latest changes into your copy.
- **Pull Request (PR):** "Here are my changes, please review and add them to the
  master." A teammate looks it over before it becomes official.

---

## Getting set up: the first time only

You'll do this once.

1. **Get access.** Ask the project owner to add you as a collaborator on the private
   repo. Until they do, GitHub won't let you in. You'll get an email invite. Accept it.

2. **Clone the repo.** This single step creates a folder on your computer and downloads
   the entire project into it (all files and full history). In Claude Code, say:
   > *"Clone our team's GitHub repo to my computer."*

   You may be asked to sign in to GitHub the first time. Just follow the prompts.

3. **Run setup.** Once cloned, open the folder in Claude Code and say:
   > *"Set up my local environment."*

   This runs `/setup-local` and configures Claude Code for your personal environment.

That's it. You now have a complete local copy, ready to work. **You never clone again.**
From here on it's the daily rhythm below.

---

## What you do, day to day

**1. Before you start: get the latest**
> *"Get the latest changes from GitHub."*

So you're building on everyone's most recent work.

**2. Start a fresh branch for what you're about to do**
> *"Start a new branch for the [screen or feature name]."*

Now you're in your own safe sandbox.

**3. Do your design work** as normal. Run skills like `/extract` or `/workshop` as needed.

**4. Save checkpoints as you go**
> *"Save my work with a note about what I changed."*

Whenever you hit a good stopping point, like saving a version in Figma.

**5. When it's ready, send it for review**
> *"Push this and open a pull request for review."*

This puts it in front of the team. Once someone approves it, your work merges into the
master and everyone gets it.

### The simple mental model

| Action | When | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Clone** | Once, at the very start | Creates your local folder and downloads everything |
| **Pull** | Every time before working | Updates your folder with the team's latest |
| **Push** | When you're ready to share | Sends your changes back up to GitHub |

Lifecycle: **clone once, then pull / work / push, over and over.**

---

## The three golden rules

1. **One owner per folder at a time.** The project is organised into track folders:
   `01-context/`, `02-design/`, `03-requirements/`, `04-feedback/`, `05-handover/`. If
   you're working in a section, check with the team before someone else digs into the
   same place simultaneously. A quick "I'm updating the card component" in chat avoids
   clashes.

2. **Coordinate before editing shared foundations.** The design library (`02-design/library/`)
   contains tokens, CSS variables, and component files. It is the shared foundation for the
   whole project. Two people editing the same file at once means one version gets lost. A
   quick heads-up avoids it.

3. **Always pull before you start, and share small changes often.** Little and frequent
   beats one giant update. Easier to review, far less likely to clash.

---

## What if something goes wrong?

- **"Two of us changed the same thing":** GitHub flags it and asks which version to
  keep. Rare, and Claude Code walks you through it. Nothing is lost.
- **"I think I broke something":** you didn't. Every version is saved forever; we can
  always roll back. Just ask Claude Code for help.
- **When in doubt, ask Claude Code:** *"I'm confused about the state of my files, can
  you explain what's going on?"* It can see exactly where things stand.

## Audit findings

**Expected-empty confirmed / anomalies**
- `03-requirements/{epics,features,stories}/`, `04-feedback/`, `01-context/{ref-local,summaries,discovery}/` — each contains only a `.gitkeep`, genuinely empty. Confirmed.
- `01-context/ref-external/links.md` — template/instructions only, no real entries. Confirmed empty.
- `01-context/project-context.md` — placeholder-only synthesis layer as expected (`last-updated: not yet run`, all manifest arrays empty).
- **Anomaly:** `01-context/decisions.md` is NOT empty — it holds a full dated (2026-07-07) planning-session log covering ADW structural changes and Zimmermann-specific decisions (component prefix TBD, web-only platform scope, etc.). This is real, substantive content that exists in `01-context/` but is not reflected anywhere in `project-context.md`'s manifest (`workshop-sessions: []`, synthesis "Not yet populated"). It's orphaned relative to the synthesis layer, though it is consistent with the file's own designed purpose (conversational-intake decisions log, separate from `/update-context`).

**Handover template gaps** (`05-handover/index.md`)
Unfilled placeholders: `[Project Name]` (title), `[Client]`, `[Lead]`, `[Stacks]`, `[AA or AAA]` (WCAG), `[DD MMM YYYY]` (Last updated), and the Build Status line still lists both options unselected (`Design & Requirements Stage | Ready for Build`). The changelog block placeholder row was never replaced. Components/Screens/Flows/Prototypes tables are all a single blank row. Requirements counts show 0 (accurate, not itself a bug, given `03-requirements/` is empty). Additionally, the Platform guardrails table links to `platform/ios/README.md` and `platform/android/README.md` (plus their annotation templates) — these don't exist; only `05-handover/platform/web/` is present, consistent with the project being web+react only. This is a dangling reference, not just unfilled text.

**Tooling & MCP wiring**
`06-tools/markitdown-mcp/` is a real, complete vendor drop: `pyproject.toml` matches upstream Microsoft `markitdown-mcp`, `src/markitdown_mcp/__main__.py` is a full 140-line implementation (FastMCP, SSE/HTTP transports, CLI), and the `Dockerfile` matches upstream. Not scaffolding. However `tests/` contains only a 4-line `__init__.py` (license header) — no actual test cases, an empty stub.
`.claude/mcp.json` registers `"command": "python", "args": ["-m", "markitdown_mcp"]`. Verified two concrete problems: (1) `python` does not resolve on this machine — only `python3` exists (`/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`); (2) `markitdown_mcp` is not installed/importable anywhere (no venv in repo, `pip show` empty) — `python3 -c "import markitdown_mcp"` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`. The config doesn't point at the vendored `src/` path directly; it silently depends on a separate `pip install -e 06-tools/markitdown-mcp[all]` step (per `MARKITDOWN_SETUP.md`'s own troubleshooting section) that hasn't happened. So right now this MCP server would fail to start. Also, `mcp.json`'s `"alwaysAllow": ["convert_document"]` names a tool that doesn't exist — the server's only tool is `convert_to_markdown`.

**Config/secrets scan**
`.claude/settings.json` — hooks reference `guard-write.sh`, `guard-bash.sh`, `on-write.sh`, all present; one MCP permission (`mcp__claude_ai_Figma__download_assets`), nothing broad. No secrets.
`.claude/settings.local.json` — untracked/gitignored, but via the user's global `~/.gitignore_global` (`**/.claude/settings.local.json`), not the repo's own `.gitignore` (which only names `CLAUDE.local.md`). Contents are just hardcoded local absolute-path `cp`/`chmod` commands for hook installation plus `npm --version` — no tokens or credentials.

**Git hooks summary**
- `guard-bash.sh` — PreToolUse: blocks `rm` on managed ADW folders and destructive git ops (`reset --hard`, `checkout --`, `clean -f`).
- `guard-write.sh` — PreToolUse: hard-blocks Writes to skill-managed files (`index.md`, `project-context.md`, `viewer.config.js`, `bmad/`, `summaries/`), soft-warns on sensitive-but-editable ones.
- `on-write.sh` — PostToolUse: logs a pending-update marker and checks spec/handover consistency (missing intent.md spec links, stale tokens→CSS sync, unindexed specs).
